lines.text: Tuesday, your agent spends an hour learning that the staging server is only reachable through the V P N.
Wednesday, a new chat begins, and the agent remembers nothing. It starts the same hour all over again.
You pay twice, in your time, and in tokens. And it happens again with every agent you add.
Agent R Q gives every workspace one shared memory. Whatever one agent learns, the others can read.
Claude saves the lesson once, as a short entry. Staging needs the V P N.
The entries hang off a small index. An agent reads the index, and opens only the entries it needs.
On the next task, Gemini or Codex loads the memory before touching anything, as a standing rule.
So the agent connects to the V P N first, and the deploy just works. No hour lost.
It works on any machine, a laptop, a server or the cloud, because the memory lives in the workspace, not in a file you copy around.
You can read, edit or delete any entry yourself. It is your project, and the memory stays honest.
Over weeks, the memory compounds. Each lesson is learned once, and then every agent starts a little further ahead.
Agents that remember. Try workspace memory at Agent R Q dot com.
